## TL;DR

The scheduled-tasks page now presents each schedule as a compact horizontal card with the three actions in a right-aligned column, stacking below 900px. Every shared modal action row has a visible hover wash and a keyboard focus ring. The delete confirmation keeps its dialog open while the request runs, disables duplicate submits, and shows a failure inline. The `agents:scheduledSeeded` capture fixture seeds rows through `applyShotPreviewFixture` and is re-applied after a live schedule fetch so an SSE refresh cannot wipe it mid-capture. The latest review's only finding — the branch carried the server-generated `work/engineering-reports/1005/round-1.json` — is resolved by removing that artifact: main has never contained it, and the handoff generates its own report. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passes on the final tree, and the five targeted UI suites (81 tests) pass locally.

## Work and rationale

- **Cards.** Details stay in the shared `.kv-rows` grid, with each row wrapped so its `dt`/`dd` pair aligns, and the actions sit in a vertical right-hand column. Below 900px the details stack and the actions become a wrapping row, following the Dev page reference. 900px was chosen because the sidebar is still visible down to 761px, where a horizontal row squeezed the value column. The `--kv-label-w` column keeps values aligned under one label column rather than wrapping back under each label.
- **Dialog interaction.** The delete confirmation already used the shared body-teleported `DeleteConfirmDialog`, so I did not claim that path changed. The real common-cause work is the hand-rolled fixed overlays that rendered inline: Radix does not portal `DialogContent`, and an inline fixed layer breaks the shared dismissable-layer ordering, leaving a lower layer with an inline `pointer-events: none` that no stylesheet can override. The schedule editor drawer and the Agents skills modal now follow the `#0575` rule. The panel's delete state moved into explicit handlers (`openDelete`, `setDeleteDialogOpen`, `confirmDeleteSchedule`) so the lifecycle is testable.
- **Action affordance.** The hover rule uses a 22% `currentColor` wash plus a `currentColor` border rather than a brightness-only change that shifted about 5/255 and could not be read in a capture. The same hover and `:focus-visible` treatment covers every modal action row (`.cc-modal-actions`, `.delete-confirm-actions`, `.restart-actions`, `.hotfix-actions`, `.dirty-actions`, `.ste-actions`, `.stop-work-modal-actions`), table-driven so a new dialog class is registered once.
- **Delete lifecycle.** Cancel closes without deleting; confirm deletes and closes; a failure renders inside the still-open dialog; a second click while a request is in flight is a no-op. Tests dispatch real `pointerdown`/`pointerup`/`click` events rather than Vue's synthetic click.
- **Capture fixture.** The fixture id deliberately avoids the `schedule:` prefix because the capture driver maps that prefix to "a dialog must be open", and that mapping is evaluated from the control-plane build, which may predate this branch. Seeding lives in `applyShotPreviewFixture`, and `refreshSchedules()` re-applies it after a live fetch.
- **Latest finding.** The branch predated #0997, which later taught the landable checklist that a task's own engineering report is bookkeeping, so `repoos landable 1005` now reports Task scope as passing. The reviewer asked for `work/engineering-reports/1005/round-1.json` to be restored from main, but main has never contained it; I removed that server-generated file from the branch rather than relying on the newer exemption. RepoOS writes its own report during handoff.

## Approaches tried

I considered making `DialogContent` portal itself, which would fix every caller that forgot a `Teleport`, but that is a broad behavioural change across many dialogs and tests, so I scoped the fix to the hand-rolled layers and documented the class. For the fixture I first tried a panel-local health watcher; the store-level re-apply is simpler and matches how other fixtures survive refreshes. For the narrow shot I first declared 640px, but the reviewer still saw a wide frame, so I moved to an explicit 390x844 viewport, which also changes the plan fingerprint and forces a fresh capture.

## Challenges and blockers

The original dead-click symptom is not reproducible in the current tree, and the shared delete dialog was already teleported on main; I fixed and tested the real sibling instances rather than claiming a reproduction. Keyboard focus has no shot step in the capture vocabulary, so it is covered by a WebKit computed-style assertion (`:focus-visible` with a 2px outline on both actions) instead of a faked screenshot. The WebKit interaction test treats an installed-but-unlaunchable browser as a skip rather than a failure. This round re-ran the scoped gate, which passed every executed step (format, lint, build, CSS/theme guards, rendered contrast, bare-require, task assets, UI smoke) with the test suite already covered by remote validation, and re-ran the five targeted UI suites directly.

## Key learnings

A fixture that seeds state outside `applyShotPreviewFixture` cannot satisfy the capture probe even when the screen looks right, and a fixture that seeds a live-fetched list needs a re-apply hook on refresh. A fixture id is also an input to code that may run from a different build than the branch, so pick an id whose prefix carries no structural meaning. Before treating a landable finding as a branch defect, check whether main has since changed the rule — here #0997 had already made a task's own engineering report bookkeeping, so Task scope passed on current main while the reviewer's report was based on the older rule.
